title: 1. Fruit flies.
text:
Question 1: What is the more common family of fruit flies to the public?




















 A. Tephritidae   B. Drosophilidiae   C. Drosophilidae   D. Tephritidiae  Submit





Question 2: What commonly makes Tephritids “bad”?


 A. They have the highest fitness   B. Being colourful means they are better at being sneaky   C. The females use their ovipositor to lay their eggs in the fruit, where larvae develop   D. They’re bigger than Drosophila, so they can do more  Submit





Question 3: What’s the other name for Tephritid flies?


 A. Peacock flies   B. Parrot flies   C. Rainbow flies   D. Robin flies  Submit





Question 4: Why are Medflies the more harsh Tephritids?


 A. They can survive in cooler temperatures compared to other Tephritids .  B. Despite using long reads, the taxonomic classifiers couldn’t resolve taxa beyond the genus level.  C. title: Microbial Sequencing Quiz
text:
Question 1: What gene is commonly targeted for bacterial community profiling?


 A. COI  B. 18S rRNA  C. 16S rRNA  D. ITS Submit





Question 2: Which sequencing approach provides the highest functional resolution?


 A. Short-read 16S rRNA sequencing  B. Long-read 16S rRNA sequencing  C. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing  D. Amplicon-based metatranscriptomics Submit





Question 3: What is a key advantage of long-read 16S rRNA sequencing compared to short-read 16S?


 A. Lower cost per base  B. Higher taxonomic resolution across the full 16S gene  C. Faster sequencing speed  D. Detects RNA viruses Submit





Question 4: I took you through a couple of papers in Medfly that have used long-read sequencing. What’s the main issue with these studies?


 A. The sequencing depth was too high, leading to data redundancy.  B. Despite using long reads, the taxonomic classifiers couldn’t resolve taxa beyond the genus level.  C. Long reads introduced large sequencing errors that prevented assembly.  D. The studies focused only on viral DNA rather than bacterial communities. Submit

title: Tephritid Microbe Functions Quiz
text:
Question 1: In Ceratitis capitata, what is one documented benefit of adding Enterobacteriaceae to the diet?


 A. Decreased lifespan and fertility  B. Enhanced development and mating success  C. Increased larval mortality  D. Reduced nitrogen metabolism Submit






Question 2: Which microbial genera in Rhagoletis pomonella are involved in purine degradation?


 A. Pseudomonas and Serratia  B. Enterobacter and Klebsiella  C. Lactobacillus and Acetobacter  D. Candidatus Erwinia and Enterococcus Submit






Question 3: What is one challenge faced in the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) related to microbiota?


 A. Microbes become pathogenic post-irradiation  B. Irradiation and mass-rearing can disrupt gut microbiota  C. Sterile males overproduce beneficial bacteria  D. Female flies reject sterile males due to microbial odour Submit






Question 4: How might probiotic supplementation improve SIT outcomes?


 A. By increasing stress and mortality rates  B. By restoring beneficial gut bacteria to enhance fitness  C. By sterilising females through microbial competition  D. By reducing energy metabolism efficiency Submit

title: Surafce sterilisation of flies
text:
Question 1: What is surface sterilisation in this context?


 A. Washing the bench surface in the lab so you don’t contaminate the fly in microbiota experiments.   B. Washing the surface of the fly to remove external microbes   C. Putting fly in bath   D. Washing the outside of the cage which you will collect flies on, to not infect its mcirobiota  Submit






Question 2: What are Tephritids commonly known as?


 A. Fake fruit flies  B. True fruit flies  C. Seed beetles  D. Flower midges Submit






Question 3: Which of the following species does NOT belong to the family Tephritidae?


 A. Ceratitis capitata  B. Bactrocera dorsalis  C. Ceratitis cosyra  D. Drosophila melanogaster Submit






Question 4: What is the main function of the female Tephritid’s ovipositor?


 A. To extract nectar from flowers  B. To puncture fruit and deposit eggs beneath the skin  C. To produce pheromones for mating  D. To digest fruit pulp Submit






Question 5: Tephritid species can be described as being:


 A. Only monophagous  B. Only polyphagous  C. Either monophagous or polyphagous  D. Neither monophagous nor polyphagous Submit






Question 6: According to the distribution map, Tephritid pests are most commonly found in:


 A. Polar regions  B. Temperate countries  C. Warmer countries  D. High-altitude environments Submit






Question 7: Which Tephritid species was listed as being found in Queensland?


 A. Bactrocera dorsalis  B. Ceratitis cosyra  C. Ceratitis capitata  D. Bactrocera tryoni Submit






Question 8: The interactive map uses circle size to represent which variable?


 A. Wing length  B. Fruit size  C. Species abundance  D. Temperature range Submit






Question 9: The “true fruit flies” belong to Tephritidae. Which family contains the so-called “fake fruit flies” like Drosophila melanogaster?


 A. Calliphoridae  B. Drosophilidae  C. Muscidae  D. Syrphidae Submit






Question 10: Which of the following statements about Tephritids is true?


 A. All Tephritids are serious agricultural pests.  B. Female Tephritids lack a specialized ovipositor.  C. Some Tephritids are beneficial, while others are pests.  D. Tephritids are primarily found in cold, mountainous regions. Submit
